questions.q: You want to change which of an option's declarations is reported as its spec (e.g. prefer the first-declared flag instead of the longest-prefix one). Which file and function do you change?
questions.answer: src/click/core.py, the `Parameter.spec` property. It returns `self.name` when `opts` is empty, else `max(self.opts, key=lambda opt: len(_split_opt(opt)[0]))`. `Option` does not override it; `Argument` overrides it to return its metavar. `_split_opt` lives in src/click/parser.py.
key_points: picks the opt with the longest prefix via _split_opt; falls back to name when opts is empty

questions.q: You want to change what an argument shows in the left column of its help row and in its error hint (e.g. 'Missing argument ...'). Where is that decided?
questions.answer: src/click/core.py, `Argument.get_help_spec(ctx)`, which returns `self.make_metavar(ctx)` (e.g. FILENAME, [FILENAME], [FILENAME]...). `Argument.get_help_record` and `Argument.get_error_hint` both call it; `get_error_hint` falls back to `self.spec` (metavar or uppercased name) when ctx is None.
key_points: get_help_record and get_error_hint go through get_help_spec

questions.q: You need to change the warning emitted when a third-party Parameter subclass still overrides `human_readable_name`, or fix which line that warning points at. Where is it?
questions.answer: src/click/core.py, `Parameter.__init_subclass__`. It checks `'human_readable_name' in cls.__dict__` and warns with DeprecationWarning, using `stacklevel=_outside_click_stacklevel(skip=("abc",))`. The stack walk is the module-level helper `_outside_click_stacklevel` in the same file, which gained the `skip` parameter because the `abc` module's frame sits between `__init_subclass__` and the user's `class` statement.
key_points: skip exists because abc's frame sits between __init_subclass__ and the class statement

questions.q: A plugin defines `class MyOpt(click.Option)` with its own `human_readable_name` property returning 'custom'. What happens at import time and at runtime after this PR?
questions.answer: Defining the class emits a DeprecationWarning ('MyOpt overrides 'human_readable_name'. Click no longer reads that property. Override 'spec' instead...'). At runtime the override has no effect: Click's error messages, deprecation messages and error hints read `spec`, not `human_readable_name`. A subclass that does not override it emits no warning.
key_points: the override has no effect because Click reads spec
subclasses without the override stay silent

questions.q: Given `@click.option('--my-option', deprecated=True)` and a user passing `--my-option hello`, what message is printed, and what did it say before this PR? Also, what does `click.Option(['-t', '--times']).human_readable_name` now return?
questions.answer: It prints `The option '--my-option' is deprecated.` to stderr (in red, plus the deprecation suffix if `deprecated` is a string); before the PR it read `The option 'my_option' is deprecated.` because it used the internal name. `human_readable_name` now emits a DeprecationWarning and returns `self.spec`, so `'--times'` instead of the old `'times'`.

questions.q: Which test files cover `spec`/`get_help_spec` for options and for arguments, and what exact command runs just the option spec tests from the repo root?
questions.answer: Options: tests/test_options.py (`test_spec`, `test_spec_with_explicit_name`, `test_help_spec`). Arguments: tests/test_arguments.py (`test_spec_and_help_spec`, `test_help_spec_matches_help_record`). Command: `python -m pytest tests/test_options.py -k spec`.
key_points: python -m pytest tests/test_options.py -k spec (or equivalent pytest -k selection)

questions.q: Where are the human_readable_name deprecation tests, how do you run them, and why would a new test that merely reads `param.human_readable_name` without `pytest.warns` fail?
questions.answer: tests/test_deprecations.py (`test_parameter_human_readable_name_deprecated`, `test_parameter_human_readable_name_override_deprecated`, `test_parameter_subclass_without_override_is_silent`). Run `python -m pytest tests/test_deprecations.py -k human_readable_name`. pyproject.toml sets `[tool.pytest.ini_options] filterwarnings = ["error"]`, so any unexpected DeprecationWarning becomes an error; wrap the access in `pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning)`.
key_points: pyproject.toml filterwarnings = ['error'] turns warnings into failures

questions.q: Why did the PR replace `human_readable_name` with a new `spec` property instead of just fixing it in place, and why does an option's spec use the longest-prefix declaration?
questions.answer: The PR separates three strings with three audiences: `decls` (what the developer passes), `spec` (what the user reads in --help and types), `name` (what Click uses internally and passes to the callback). `human_readable_name` returned the internal `name` for options but the metavar for arguments, so it mixed audiences; changing its value in place would silently break callers, so a new name was added and the old one deprecated (removal in 9.0) with a warning. Spec uses the longest-prefix declaration because that is the same declaration Click derives `name` from, so spec and name stay consistent (`-t, --times` -> spec `--times`, name `times`), regardless of declaration order.
key_points: human_readable_name returned internal name for options (inconsistent with arguments)
deprecated rather than changed silently; removed in Click 9.0
longest prefix matches how name is derived, so spec and name agree

task.prompt: `Parameter.spec` (added in #3877) is how the user spells a parameter on the command line, but documentation generators that walk `Context.to_info_dict()` can't see it: `Parameter.to_info_dict()` only exposes the internal `name` and the raw `opts`. Please add a `"spec"` key to the dict returned by `Parameter.to_info_dict()`, holding the value of the parameter's `spec` property (so `--times` for `-t/--times`, `FILENAME` for `argument('filename')`, the metavar if one is given, and whatever a subclass's `spec` override returns). It must not go through the deprecated `human_readable_name`. It should show up for every parameter in `Command`/`Context.to_info_dict()` output, including the automatic `--help` option. Update the existing expectations in tests/test_info_dict.py, add a `versionchanged:: 8.6.0` note to the docstring and a CHANGES.md entry.
